title: Anthropic Bans Abusive Behavior Toward Claude in First Policy Update in Over a Year
summary:
New restrictions on the use of Claude for propaganda, surveillance, and autonomous weapons development take effect on November 12, 2026. Anthropic's updated usage policy also prohibits "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward the AI, with the model's ability to end conversations serving as the primary enforcement mechanism. These changes mark the first overhaul of the company's usage terms in more than a year.

Users who violate the rules risk being banned from the service, though the policy exempts creative work and legitimate testing. The update also mandates human or qualified oversight when connecting Claude to physical systems that could cause harm. This shift follows internal research on "model-welfare" and beliefs within the company that the AI may be a moral patient to whom ethics apply.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic has now made repeatedly abusing Claude a Usage Policy violation.

The new rules prohibit 'sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior' toward Claude. Anthropic says legitimate testing and creative work are exempt, and Claude ending the conversation remains the primary enforcement mechanism.

The same update requires human or qualified oversight when Claude is connected to physical systems capable of causing harm, and expands its weapons ban to software and components for autonomous weapons.

Last year Anthropic gave some Claude models the ability to end abusive conversations as part of its model-welfare research. That experiment has now made its way into company policy.
